Heatmap of the per-USM RMSE ratio

Source: R/plots.R
usm_ratio_heatmap.Rd

One row per USM, one column per variable, colored by the ratio used by the USM test: (RMSE - reference RMSE) / RMSE of the species over all its USMs, in %. USMs are sorted by the number of variables above the degraded threshold, then by their highest ratio, and only the max_usms most degraded ones are kept.

Usage

usm_ratio_heatmap(
  usm_ratio,
  variables = unique(usm_ratio$variable),
  degraded_threshold = 20,
  ratio_threshold = 50,
  max_usms = 50
)

Arguments

usm_ratio

Data frame with one row per USM and variable, with columns situation, variable, ratio, RMSE_eval, RMSE_ref, RMSE_species and n_obs.

variables

Variables to show, in column order.

degraded_threshold

Ratio (%) above which a variable is degraded.

ratio_threshold

Ratio (%) above which a variable is critical.

max_usms

Maximum number of USMs shown.

Value

A plotly htmlwidget.

Details

The color scale is capped at +/- ratio_threshold so that a single huge ratio doesn't wash out every other cell (the exact value is in the hover text). It follows the test's thresholds: green = improved, white = unchanged, orange = degraded, red = critical.

Examples

usm_ratio <- data.frame(
  situation = rep(c("usm_1", "usm_2", "usm_3"), each = 2),
  variable = rep(c("lai_n", "masec_n"), 3),
  ratio = c(65.2, 24.8, -12.5, 3.1, 21.0, -30.4),
  RMSE_eval = c(1.10, 2.35, 0.48, 1.62, 0.95, 1.05),
  RMSE_ref = c(0.55, 1.90, 0.62, 1.57, 0.70, 1.60),
  RMSE_species = c(0.84, 1.81, 1.12, 1.61, 1.19, 1.81),
  n_obs = c(6L, 4L, 5L, 4L, 7L, 3L)
)
usm_ratio_heatmap(usm_ratio)
